To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of 5% poly phosphate to pork loins, prior to cooking, can improve the eating quality of pork loin steaks.

polyphosphate injection into pork loin improves tenderness, juici-ness and water holding capacity but also increases the intensity of abnormal flavour, which may be due to increased Maillard browning.

polyphosphate injection into pork loin steaks can increase the tenderness and juiciness of the meat when cooked to high temperatures (80°C), but the effect is less than that which can be achieved by cooking the meat to a lower temperature (72.5°C).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods to improve the eating quality of pork.

the development and application of novel technologies to improve the eating quality of pork and the development of a `value added' pork product that can be produced from the same raw material as the `standard' product.
the development of a new technology to improve the eating quality of pork and the results indicate that the technology is feasible.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of polyphosphate to improve pork eating quality can be justified, but the use of high cooking temperatures to achieve the same effect is not.
the addition of polyphosphate to pork loin steaks improved eating quality, particularly when the steaks were cooked to a higher centre temperature.

the injection of water and poly-phosphate into pork to produce a more tender and juicy cooked product is feasible and that the effects are greater than those that can normally be obtained by changing diets and breeds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
polyphosphate injection is an effective means of improving the eating quality of pork.
injection of polyphosphate into meat can improve eating quality but that this improvement is dependent on the cooking method.
polyphosphate injection is a very effective way of increasing juiciness and improving water holding of cooked pork, but that it also increases abnormal flavours and reduces pork flavour.
The main takeaway from our work is that

polyphosphate can be used to reduce cooking losses, and hence improve tenderness, and to improve juiceness of pork steaks, but that it does so by reducing pork flavour intensity and increasing abnormal flavour intensity.
polyphosphate can be used to improve pork eating quality but that this may be limited to a relatively narrow window of cooking temperatures.
it is not possible to improve eating quality of pork in a single step.
